summary: A neighborhood feature profiling young changemakers who led community projects between September and December 2023. Their work spans recycling, volunteering technology, homelessness advocacy, environmental cleanup and education, cultural exchange, community gardening, and winter clothing drives. The piece argues that supporting youth initiatives builds active citizenship and solidarity.
one_line: Profiles of teenage community leaders in 2023 whose environmental, advocacy, volunteering, and inclusion projects are improving their neighborhood.
key_facts: On September 4, 2023, young people met at the East End Youth Center to discuss the neighborhood's future; the roundtable was led by Sarah Mendez, a 16-year-old high school junior.
Sarah Mendez previously launched a successful recycling program at her school and advocates sustainable practices.

On September 15, 2023, 17-year-old Jacob Liu unveiled the app "VolunNear" at the Midtown Library; it connects local businesses and residents with volunteer opportunities matching their skills and interests.
Jacob Liu built "VolunNear" in partnership with local tech mentors and businesses that offered support.
On September 22, 2023, Ava Thompson, a 14-year-old advocate for the homeless, organized a rally at City Hall and is sparking discussion of potential legislative reforms.
Ava Thompson identified the need for policy changes through her volunteer work at local shelters.
On October 3, 2023, 15-year-old Nicole Zhang led a cleanup at Crescent Lake Park with more than a hundred volunteers.
Nicole Zhang intends to introduce environmental education programs in local schools; local businesses donated supplies and city officials are considering her environmental curriculum.
Omar Ahmed, an 18-year-old refugee who arrived on September 30, 2023, founded the "Unity Through Diversity" initiative, which organizes cultural exchange events and language classes.

On November 8, 2023, 16-year-old Miguel Rivera presented a community garden model at the Southwest Neighborhood Assembly, aimed at teaching nutrition, providing fresh produce to those in need, and creating a neighborhood gathering space.
Miguel Rivera's gardens are planned for empty lots and have the backing of local leaders.
On December 1, 2023, 17-year-old Emily Martin spearheaded a "Winter Warmth Drive" that filled multiple shelters with winter clothing and drew volunteers of various age groups.
